messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Page: @oncall-db — High error rate surfaced after recent deploy (canary reported OK). Please acknowledge.

alex: ACK. seeing increased 5xx on write paths, small spike first, now ~2.5% of global requests failing. throwing `relation "user_features" does not exist` in a couple of services.

morgan: same, proxy errors in front-end for a subset of tenants. query failures started ~3m after canary finished. canary logs looked fine.

jamie: I looked at deploy logs — the schema migration ran in canary, added a column with a non-null default that triggers a table rewrite on large table. canary small shard, prod bigger -> that's probably it.

oncall-db: I'm on it. can everyone stop further rollouts please? @@deploy-bot hold all deploys

oncall-db: SQL error example from svc-payment: `ERROR: column "payment_metadata_v2" does not exist at character 215` — means code expects new column while migration not fully applied to all read replicas.

luis: @oncall-db can you share the migration DDL?

oncall-db: DDL (from release):
```sql
ALTER TABLE user_features ADD COLUMN payment_metadata_v2 JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb;
-- followup backfill job scheduled as a long-running task
```

jamie: aha, default triggers table rewrite on older PG versions. backfill job blocked behind row-level locks from slow queries.

alex: customer impact: SLO error budget burn: some downstream endpoints returning 500/503; handful of larger tenants seeing degraded writes. No PII leaked.

morgan: @support-bot can you start a customer-impact thread and tag mid-market customers? Need to prepare a brief.

support-bot: Started incident-customer-updates channel and DM to CSMs. Draft: "We’re investigating an issue causing intermittent write failures for some tenants after an internal deploy. Engineers are actively working on mitigation — will update in 30m."

oncall-db: Immediate plan: (1) Pause traffic to new code path via feature-flag kill-switch, (2) stop any further schema-altering rollouts, (3) coordinate manual chunked backfill to avoid table rewrite.

alex: how do we flip the flag?

oncall-db: Run the internal kill script: `./ff-toggle --org all --flag payment_metadata_v2_enabled --off --reason "deploy-induced errors"`

morgan: I flipped the flag for global traffic. Confirming decreased errors in 30s window. :white_check_mark:

jamie: Nice. That prevented new writers from assuming column exists. But the migration already started on some DB hosts — need to ensure replicas finish or admin abort if needed.

oncall-db: On replicas, the ALTER completed on ~30% of hosts, others pending. We need to avoid partial schema exposure. Options: roll forward (finish backfill carefully) or roll back code that expects column (we already killed flag so code should be safe). Recommend pausing migration and resume as chunked.

luis: How do we pause the migration? It's a built-in migration task kicked off by release-controller.

oncall-db: I called release-controller and paused migration job ID 98765. It’s now in WAIT_PAUSED.

oncall-db: Next: spawn a small team to perform safe backfill: chunked updates using `UPDATE ... WHERE id BETWEEN x AND y` in parallel, avoiding long table rewrites. Also ensure statement_timeout set low on backfill worker.

ajamie: (typo) jamie: I'll own chunking plan with @luis. Alex — can you keep an eye on customer traffic and SLO dashboards?

alex: on it. adding a dashboard overlay now.

morgan: on-call handoff note: I have to go in 20m, @alex will be primary after that, @jamie second.

oncall-db: Assigning tasks:
- jamie: chunked backfill plan and runbook (ETA 15m)
- luis: execute first chunk and monitor locks (ETA 25m)
- alex: customer comms + SLO monitoring (ongoing)
- morgan: prepare rollback artifacts if chunking fails (standby)

luis: First chunk executed: `UPDATE user_features SET payment_metadata_v2 = '{}' WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 250000` — completed in 4m, lock time ~0.9s median. No visible replica lag.

alex: error rate down from 2.5% -> 0.4% after flag flip + chunk 1. Good signal.

jamie: Great. proceeding with parallel chunk workers with small batch size and random sleep to reduce contention. Please avoid full-table rewrite statements.

oncall-db: Note: some legacy read-only replicas still report old schema; switching read traffic away from those replicas for now. Routed read-only traffic to newer hosts.

morgan: Can we keep a slow roll of the migration instead of aborting? Might finish earlier than many chunk jobs.

oncall-db: Risky: the rewrite will cause full table lock for seconds -> seconds * heavy QPS = client errors. Chunking is safer.

luis: Running chunk 2/12. ETA 18m for batch of 250k.

support-bot: CSMs updated with a 30m ETA for next customer update. They asked for root cause once we have it.

alex: Monitoring: error budget burn stopped. I'm going to mark the incident as "mitigated" once chunking finished and errors stable <0.5% for 15m.

oncall-db: Agreed. Postmortem actions while this is fresh:
- Change migration to `ADD COLUMN ... NULL` then backfill then `SET NOT NULL` as a separate step.
- Avoid non-null defaults that force table rewrites.
- Add pre-deploy check for table size and potential rewrite cost.
- Add automatic feature-flag guard for any migration that exposes schema to app code mid-rollout.

jamie: I'll open a follow-up ticket and link to this thread. Tagging infra and release teams.

morgan: Handoff: I'm off now — alex you're primary. Please escalate to SRE lead if we see >1% errors for 10m.

alex: acknowledged. continuing to monitor. will post timeline and postmortem link when available.

luis: Chunk 5 complete. No regression. Running final batches.

oncall-db: Migration job resumed in chunked mode and finished on all hosts at 2412345790.

alex: Confirming stable metrics, error rate <0.2% for 20m. Marking mitigated.

support-bot: Notified CSMs and updated incident-customer-updates channel with mitigation note.

jamie: Postmortem TODOs already created and assigned. Thanks everyone for fast responses.

alex: closing the temporary incident channel in 1h after postmortem draft. Good work. :tada:
